prompt: I keep seeing people quote the Book of Five Rings but I've never actually read it. What's the Fire book actually about, and what does 'the body of a rock' mean? Also — is any of it useful for what I'm dealing with, which is a competitor who just launched a near-identical product at 40% of our price and is undercutting us at every renewal?
assertions: Explains the Fire book accurately as being about engagement: position, timing, and initiative
Explains the three sen (ken no sen / tai no sen / tai tai no sen)
Explains 'body of a rock' (iwao no mi) as immovable spirit arising from mastery, and places it correctly as the closing teaching of the Fire book
Applies at least two named Fire-book tactics to the price-undercutting situation with concrete moves
Does not attribute Sun Tzu or Hagakure material to Musashi
Contains no fabricated direct quotations attributed to Musashi
Answers the user's actual competitive problem rather than staying in 17th-century Japan
No samurai cosplay: no pseudo-archaic voice, invented Japanese, or closing haiku
